question.problem: Given that the $5$th term of a geometric sequence is $-125$, and the common ratio is $5,$ find the formula for the $n$th term.
question.worked_solution:
The common ratio is $r=5,$ so we can start writing the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & ={a}_{1}\cdot {5}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

However, we still need to figure out the first term ${a}_{1}.$ We know that the $5$th term is ${a}_{5}=-125,$ so we can solve for the first term as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{5} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {5}^{5-1} \\ -125 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {5}^{4} \\ -{5}^{3} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {5}^{4} \\ -\frac{1}{5} & ={a}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that we know the first term is ${a}_{1}=-\frac{1}{5},$ we can complete the formula for the $n$th term of the sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {5}^{n-1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}\cdot {5}^{n-1} \\  & =-\frac{{5}^{n-1}}{5} \\  & =-{5}^{n-2}\end{aligned}
$$
